problem.title: Zero-Downtime Column Renames with Expand-and-Contract
problem.prompt: A 40-pod Kubernetes deployment (`maxSurge: 25%`, `maxUnavailable: 0`) running a Python/SQLAlchemy service against MySQL 8.0 executes a rolling update from v2.0 to v2.1. An initContainer on the first v2.1 pod runs `ALTER TABLE customers RENAME COLUMN user_phone TO phone_e164;` on a 25M-row table. Immediately, all 40 existing v2.0 pods fail with `OperationalError: (1054, "Unknown column 'user_phone' in 'field list'")`, halting the readiness-gated rollout and leaving the cluster in a split-brain outage. Design a zero-downtime column rename workflow for rolling deployments on MySQL 8.0.
requirements: Support v2.0 and v2.1 pods running concurrently on the same MySQL 8.0 table for the full rollout duration
Complete the rename without blocking 3,000 QPS of live reads and writes on the 25M-row `customers` table
Eliminate initContainer race conditions across parallel pod startups
Ensure clean rollback to v2.0 if v2.1 fails readiness or canary checks
constraints: MySQL 8.0 InnoDB with 25M rows (~18 GB table size)
Zero downtime; metadata locks must stay under 1 second

stages.learnerPrompt: Why did `RENAME COLUMN` break the Kubernetes rolling update even though MySQL 8.0 performs renames as an instant metadata operation?

referenceMaterial.summary: Metadata speed does not solve application-level schema skew: v2.0 pods still issue SQL referencing `user_phone`, which immediately ceases to exist.
approachSteps: Explain that `maxSurge: 25%, maxUnavailable: 0` guarantees v2.0 and v2.1 overlap.
Show how `initContainer` execution raced and broke all 40 live v2.0 pods.
Note that failed readiness probes halt the rolling update mid-flight.
tradeOffs: Zero-downtime rolling updates require N and N-1 schema compatibility
alternatives: Take a maintenance window and scale replicas to 0 before renaming (violates zero-downtime constraint)
failureModes: initContainer migrations running concurrently across multiple surging pods

stages.learnerPrompt: Write the MySQL 8.0 Expand DDL, trigger logic, and Kubernetes migration orchestration needed to rename `user_phone` to `phone_e164` with zero downtime.
Walk through the `ALGORITHM=INSTANT` expand script, null-safe `BEFORE UPDATE` trigger, and v2.2 contract cleanup.

referenceMaterial.summary: Add `phone_e164` with `ALGORITHM=INSTANT`, synchronize both columns via `BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE` triggers using `<=>`, backfill in batches, and drop `user_phone` in v2.2.
approachSteps: Run Expand in a single K8s pre-upgrade Job with `lock_wait_timeout = 2`.
Use `<=>` in `BEFORE UPDATE` to detect whether v2.0 or v2.1 changed the value.
Backfill 25M rows in 2,000-row batches and add indexes with `LOCK=NONE`.
tradeOffs: Requires two releases (v2.1 + v2.2) to complete the rename cleanly
alternatives: If `phone_e164` is only read and never written directly until v2.2, use a MySQL `VIRTUAL` generated column instead of triggers
failureModes: Using `!=` instead of `<=>` in the `UPDATE` trigger fails when either column transitions from `NULL` to non-null

stages.learnerPrompt: When could you use a MySQL `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (user_phone) VIRTUAL` column instead of `BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE` triggers?

referenceMaterial.summary: A `VIRTUAL` generated column avoids triggers and backfill entirely if v2.1 only *reads* `phone_e164`, but cannot be written to directly by `INSERT/UPDATE`.
approachSteps: Virtual generated columns compute `phone_e164` on read with zero storage overhead.
However, MySQL rejects `INSERT INTO customers (phone_e164) VALUES (...)` on generated columns.
Therefore, triggers are required when v2.1 must write to `phone_e164` while v2.0 still writes to `user_phone`.
tradeOffs: Virtual columns are instant and trigger-free, but force v2.1 to still write to the old column name
alternatives: Use an updatable SQL `VIEW` (`customers_v2`) if the application can target a versioned table/view name
failureModes: Attempting to write to a generated column throws `ERROR 3105: The value specified for generated column is not allowed`

stages.learnerPrompt: What happens if a long-running analytics query is holding a `SHARED_READ` metadata lock on `customers` when your `ALTER TABLE` runs?

referenceMaterial.summary: MySQL's Metadata Lock (MDL) queue gives `ALTER TABLE` priority over new `SELECT/UPDATE`s; without `lock_wait_timeout`, all 3,000 QPS queue behind the analytics query.
approachSteps: Trace the MDL pileup: Analytics `SELECT` -> `ALTER TABLE` waits -> all 3,000 QPS OLTP queries block.
Set `SET SESSION lock_wait_timeout = 2;` so the DDL fails fast instead of blocking traffic.
Retry the DDL with exponential backoff until the analytics query finishes.
referenceMaterial.codeSnippet:
SET SESSION lock_wait_timeout = 2;
ALTER TABLE customers ADD COLUMN phone_e164 VARCHAR(20) NULL, ALGORITHM=INSTANT;
tradeOffs: The migration job may need 2–3 automated retries during busy hours, which is far safer than an MDL outage
alternatives: Use `gh-ost` or `pt-online-schema-change` for non-instant schema changes on large tables
failureModes: Default MySQL `lock_wait_timeout` is 31,536,000 seconds (1 year), guaranteeing an outage if an `ALTER` blocks

stages.learnerPrompt: How should Kubernetes run database migrations so 10 surging pods never race on Flyway/Alembic locks?

referenceMaterial.summary: Execute migrations in a dedicated single-pod Kubernetes `Job` (Helm `pre-upgrade` hook or ArgoCD `PreSync` hook) before updating the `Deployment`.
referenceMaterial.codeSnippet:
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: customers-db-migrate-v21
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/hook: PreSync
spec:
  backoffLimit: 2
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
        - name: alembic
          image: payments-api:v2.1
          command: ["alembic", "upgrade", "head"]
tradeOffs: Separates migration lifecycle from pod lifecycle, requiring CI/CD hook support
alternatives: Use a distributed advisory lock (`GET_LOCK` in MySQL) if migrations must remain in-app
failureModes: If `ttlSecondsAfterFinished` is omitted, old migration Jobs accumulate in the namespace

spark.summary: A rolling Kubernetes deployment renamed `user_phone` to `phone_e164` in v2.1, crashing all remaining v2.0 pods for 14 minutes with `Unknown column` SQL errors.
spark.keyTakeaway: Never rename a live column in place during a rolling deploy; use additive columns, generated/triggered sync, or updatable views across two releases.

Design a zero-downtime column rename workflow for rolling deployments on MySQL 8.0.
requirements: Support v2.0 and v2.1 pods running concurrently on the same MySQL 8.0 table for the full rollout duration
Complete the rename without blocking 3,000 QPS of live reads and writes on the 25M-row `customers` table

concept.whyItMatters: Rolling deployments inherently run old (N-1) and new (N) pods simultaneously; any in-place column rename breaks N-1 pods immediately and wedges Kubernetes readiness probes, halting the rollout mid-flight.
whenToUse: Renaming or changing the data type of columns in tables actively queried by rolling Kubernetes/ECS workloads
Refactoring legacy ORM models (SQLAlchemy, Hibernate, ActiveRecord) without maintenance windows
whenNotToUse: Renaming columns on an unreferenced staging table or a brand-new table created in the same PR
keyPoints: Replace `RENAME COLUMN` with a 3-release Expand -> Migrate -> Contract workflow
On MySQL 8.0, adding a nullable column uses `ALGORITHM=INSTANT` (metadata-only, <10 ms)
Use `BEFORE INSERT` and `BEFORE UPDATE` triggers (or MySQL generated columns when only read-aliasing is needed) to keep old and new columns synchronized
Never run schema migrations in Kubernetes `initContainers`; use a single-execution pre-deploy `Job` with `backoffLimit: 1`

tradeOffs.factor: Sync Triggers + Backfill vs. Updatable View
tradeOffs.pro: Triggers work seamlessly with existing indexes and ORMs without altering table names
tradeOffs.con: Requires a throttled backfill of the 25M existing rows before dropping the old column

tradeOffs.pro: Runs once deterministically before any v2.1 pod starts, avoiding 10-pod migration lock races
tradeOffs.con: Adds a separate Helm hook / ArgoCD `PreSync` step to the deployment manifest

failureModes.name: Metadata Lock (MDL) Pileup
failureModes.description: In MySQL, an `ALTER TABLE` waiting on one long-running `SELECT` blocks all subsequent queries on `customers` in the MDL queue
failureModes.mitigation: Set `SET SESSION lock_wait_timeout = 2;` before `ALTER TABLE` and use `ALGORITHM=INSTANT` for additive columns

failureModes.name: initContainer Migration Race
failureModes.description: 10 surging v2.1 pods start concurrently and race on migration locks, causing CrashLoopBackOff
failureModes.mitigation: Move migrations to a dedicated Helm `pre-upgrade` / ArgoCD `PreSync` Job

failureModes.name: Rollout Deadlock
failureModes.description: Breaking v2.0 pods fails their readiness probes or new pods fail to pass health checks, leaving Kubernetes stuck with 0 healthy replicas
failureModes.mitigation: Preserve 100% N-1 column compatibility until all v2.0 pods are terminated and drained

commonMistakes: Assuming `ALTER TABLE ... RENAME COLUMN` is safe because it is `ALGORITHM=INSTANT` in MySQL 8.0—metadata speed does not prevent application SQL breakage
Running migrations inside `initContainers` of a multi-replica `Deployment`
Using `SELECT *` or SQLAlchemy `autoload_with` reflection without explicit column lists, which breaks when columns are added or dropped
Forgetting to backfill historical rows before switching v2.1 reads to `phone_e164`

sections.content:
## The Problem

During a rolling update of 40 Kubernetes pods from v2.0 to v2.1, the first surging v2.1 pod executed `ALTER TABLE customers RENAME COLUMN user_phone TO phone_e164;` inside an `initContainer`. Even though MySQL 8.0 executed the rename in milliseconds, all 40 live v2.0 pods immediately threw `OperationalError 1054: Unknown column 'user_phone'`.

Because `maxUnavailable: 0` was configured and v2.0 pods began failing readiness checks while v2.1 pods were still starting, the rollout wedged into a 14-minute outage.

## Requirements & Constraints

- **Concurrent Compatibility**: v2.0 (`user_phone`) and v2.1 (`phone_e164`) must both read and write accurately during the rolling window.
- **Table Scale**: 25M rows (~18 GB) in MySQL 8.0 InnoDB at 3,000 QPS.
- **Lock Ceiling**: Metadata locks must never exceed 1–2 seconds.
- **Orchestration**: Migrations must run once before pods roll, not inside `initContainers`.

## Migration & Backfill Math

- **Expand DDL**: `ADD COLUMN phone_e164 VARCHAR(20) NULL, ALGORITHM=INSTANT` updates only the InnoDB data dictionary (~5 ms, zero table copy).
- **Backfill**: 25,000,000 rows in 2,000-row primary-key range batches at 5,000 rows/s:
  - Duration: `25,000,000 / 5,000 = 5,000 seconds` (~83 minutes) with `< 5%` InnoDB buffer pool impact.
- **Index Creation**: `ADD INDEX idx_phone_e164 (phone_e164), ALGORITHM=INPLACE, LOCK=NONE` builds the secondary index online without blocking writes.

data.title: Zero-Downtime MySQL Column Rename Across Rolling Deploys

edges.label: 1. ADD COLUMN INSTANT
edges.title: Expand Schema
edges.description: Add nullable phone_e164 with ALGORITHM=INSTANT and attach INSERT/UPDATE sync triggers.

edges.label: 2. Backfill 25M rows
edges.title: Throttled Backfill
edges.description: Copy user_phone to phone_e164 in 2k-row PK batches, then add online index (LOCK=NONE).

edges.label: 3. Write user_phone
edges.title: N-1 Traffic Continuity
edges.description: Draining v2.0 pods continue writing user_phone; trigger mirrors values to phone_e164.

edges.label: 4. Write phone_e164
edges.title: N Traffic Cutover
edges.description: New v2.1 pods read/write phone_e164; trigger mirrors values back to user_phone for safe rollback.

edges.label: 5. Contract in v2.2
edges.title: Drop Legacy Column
edges.description: In v2.2 after v2.0 is gone, drop triggers and DROP COLUMN user_phone, ALGORITHM=INSTANT.

data.caption: Bidirectional triggers and ALGORITHM=INSTANT keep v2.0 and v2.1 pods 100% compatible throughout the rolling update.

sections.content:
## Failure Handling

- **MDL Contention**: `SET SESSION lock_wait_timeout = 2` ensures `ALTER TABLE` aborts cleanly in 2s instead of queuing behind a long query and blocking 3,000 QPS.
- **Update Edge Case**: Using MySQL's null-safe equality (`<=>`) in `trg_customers_upd` accurately detects which column was modified by the caller, even when setting a phone number to `NULL`.
- **Rollback Safety**: Rolling back to v2.0 at any point during or after the v2.1 rollout works immediately because `user_phone` remains populated and indexed.

## Final Architecture Summary

Eliminate rolling-deployment column-rename outages by moving migrations out of `initContainers` into a single pre-deploy Job and executing a **3-step Expand-Backfill-Contract** flow: (1) add `phone_e164` with **`ALGORITHM=INSTANT`** and **`lock_wait_timeout = 2`** plus bidirectional `BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE` triggers; (2) backfill 25M rows in 2k-row keyset batches and add indexes with **`ALGORITHM=INPLACE, LOCK=NONE`**; (3) roll out v2.1 safely alongside v2.0, then drop triggers and `user_phone` in v2.2.
